cycles.method: static: tools/build/cycle_count.py's measure and verify (the marker is a no-op) on filter.asm, the per-sample loop to eu_loopend with its per-sample call of eu_denominator (straight-line, 43 words; the file declares CYCLES_FORWARD_BRANCHES), the worse of the two mode loops: 182 cycles/sample (AMP's loop 25). The per-block setup is outside the loop and not in this floor. measured: modules/euclid/perf.py bench, benchmark_reverbs.run as benchmark_stock_dsp.py runs it (one instance per core at positions 0 and 4, audio at X:0, 4,096 blocks of 16 frames, the null stub's peak subtracted) on a private native image built from this source by build_bus (Euclid in the space of SPRING REV and PLATE REV; image 0c23ac7d...), through the stock effects' cases (fixed, the moving-knob pattern, a trig split at every position 1-15) plus RATE 1/32 with every split, every TYPE with every OUT at RATE 1/32, and MIX 0: 54 cases. Worst 187.75 executed instructions/sample (the moving pattern with a split at frame 1; 179.94 unsplit); no case clipped. Executed instructions in dsp_host, not chip cycles. The cycle scan models 223.38 chip cycles a sample at RATE 1/32, stalls included (sdk/cycle-scan/records/euclid.json), and the owner's MKII read +3.1 points of the T1-4 DSP meter in use with a +5.9 peak, about 267 cycles a sample at the peak (development twin cd450fed of base 0.8.2, 25 November 2026, evidence/cpu-price.json). Only the DSP filter runs here: the ColdFire engine that publishes the modulated cutoff as FREQ is replaced by the knob rows.

stock.baseline: out/stock_dsp_bench/results.json from benchmark_stock_dsp.py on the owner's OS 1.40C (FILTER 236.06, SPRING REV 257.50, DJ EQ 293.38 unsplit). FILTER, SPRING REV and DJ EQ then ran on the stock image through Euclid's cases (fixed, moving, a trig split at every position 1-15): their unsplit figures reproduce results.json exactly; with splits FILTER 284.88, SPRING REV 314.19, DJ EQ 330.94.
stock.justification: FILTER is the stock effect closest in function: Euclid is a two-pole filter (LP, BP, HP, NOTCH) or an amplitude modulator whose cutoff or gain a rhythm moves. Under the same cases Euclid's worst, 187.75, is 0.66x FILTER's 284.88, 0.60x SPRING REV's 314.19 (the cost target for new FX) and 0.57x DJ EQ's 330.94, the dearest stock effect; unsplit 179.94 against 236.06, 257.50 and 293.38.

stress.method: modules/euclid/perf.py stress, after modules/bbd/perf.py's: stress_project.py needs an Octatrack template project, so the same load is driven straight into dsp_host on the private native image (0c23ac7d...): Euclid on FX2 of all eight tracks (four per core) behind CHORUS on every FX1; per block three LFOs (sine, triangle, square) on Euclid's FREQ, DEPTH and DECAY and CHORUS's first three slots, and a new random value on every named slot of both effects each sixteenth at 120 BPM: 20 slots changed per step (Euclid's twelve, CHORUS's eight), TYPE, OUT and RATE included so the modes switch under load; trig splits of 1, 3, 7, 8, 12 and 15 frames on six tracks; eight different stems (drums, a full-level chord, noise bursts, a 20 Hz-20 kHz sweep, a full-scale square, impulses, DC steps, plucks) for 2 s plus a 2 s tail; dsp_host -guard 0x4000 -guard-shared -dirty 0x5a. Result: host exit 0, no hang; Euclid's eight instances 0 stray writes and 0 clobbers (the stock CHORUSes write their own scratch, 0 clobbers); 16 guarded instances; per-core peak 1907.8 and 1906.8 executed instructions/sample with all sixteen effects. It exercises the DSP side only: the firmware's LFO and lock delivery, Euclid's ColdFire engine, Part switches and the ColdFire side are not in it.
